gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many times each pick needs charging across one 28-day cycle. Temperature-based cycle tracking needs the device worn every night, and the Apple Watch SE 3's 18-hour rating works out to about 37 charges per cycle, against about 3 to 4 for the Garmin Lily 2 Active, the Fitbit Air or the Oura Ring 5.
standout_why: I could not open the three cited rivals (womenshealthmag.com, goodhousekeeping.com, wired.com): WebFetch is blocked on those domains and curl needed approval, so I can't say whether they hold either figure. wearablebeat.com returned 403. kudomax.com (result 9) already works out a 3-year cost including subscription for the Fitbit Air ($99.99) and the Oura Ring 5 ($608.97 = 399 + 3 × 69.99), so the cost-of-ownership idea is only partly new. The new part is a 2-year cost covering the Lily 2 Active, plus charges per 28-day cycle, which nothing I opened works out.
decides: This backs the Lily 2 Active as the small-wrist pick: $299.99 with no fee, against $538.98 over 2 years for the Oura Ring 5. It also costs the Apple Watch SE 3 points for cycle tracking, because it needs about 37 charges per 28-day cycle, which interrupts the overnight wear that wrist-temperature cycle estimates rely on. For the Fitbit Air, the free tier already includes Readiness, sleep stages and HRV, so its 2-year cost can honestly be $99.99, or $299.97 with Premium.
